findings.reason: the plan must state that the fixture's merge consumes the remote-tracking ref and add a control that passing the lagging local branch fails, otherwise a node that implements the local ref passes the section's whole gate while the defect the section exists to prevent survives.
findings.text: the fixture holds "a local `main` left behind the remote-tracking ref" but none of the four assertions distinguishes the remote-tracking ref from the local branch, and the plan does not say which ref the fixture's "merge of an integration branch" consumes; if that merge consumes the local branch, `own_changed_paths(..., integration_ref="main")` returns exactly the same path set as `origin/main` and all four assertions plus the two-dot negative control still pass, so the sentence added in this revision ("never a local branch, which can lag behind it and let the integration branch's commits back in") is asserted by nothing

findings.reason: the deliverable needs the unreadable-history contract and a fixture variant asserting it, because as written the repair can silently widen the very carry it is meant to make safe.
findings.text: `own_changed_paths` is specified to "return the paths changed by commits reachable from `tip` but not from `older` or `integration_ref`" with no statement of what it returns when `git rev-list` cannot run (a tree without an `origin` remote, an unfetched or missing remote-tracking ref), whereas the neighbouring `_changed_paths_between` documents `None` as its fail-safe precisely because an uncomparable history "cannot be shown to change no runtime source"; with a bare `[]` on failure, `review_head_move` yields empty `paths`, `changes_runtime_source([])` is False, `touches_delivered_work` stays False, and `carry_review_forward` re-stamps the stored review onto a head whose delta was never read
